chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from 'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both) who said:

Regarding the woman who menstruates once every three months, or every six months, or every seven months, and the istihadah (continuous bleeding) woman, and the one who has not yet reached puberty, and the one who menstruates once and then stops, and the one who has no hope of bearing children, and the one whose menstruation has ceased but claims she has not yet reached menopause, and the one who sees yellowish discharge from menstruation that is not regular, he mentioned that the waiting period ('iddah) for all of these is three months.

key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةِ: The woman with continuous uterine bleeding (istihadah)

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for women with irregular menstruation or menopause in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes a unified three-month waiting period ('iddah) for women with irregular menstruation, pre-pubertal girls, and post-menopausal women, resolving the diversity of cases under a single legal principle. It reflects the Shia scholarly approach to *istihadah* and *iddah*, emphasizing that the passage of time serves as the primary indicator of purity when menstrual cycles are unpredictable or absent. This ruling ensures clarity in marital status transitions for these specific categories, aligning with the broader jurisprudential framework found in the *Sahih* hadith collections.
